analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md). There are no code, workflow or config changes, so no runtime security behavior changes.

prefix-cache.md: the patch excerpt shows the recurrent checkpoint bank gate now includes a 'plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner'. A new `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks` flag captures only at multiples of the fixed prefill chunk. This extends the prefix-cache documentation under T-041 (TB-007, A-001). The excerpt is truncated, and the source code behind the claim (the Nemotron Super recurrent bank owner) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. The surrounding head text (lines 442-862) is unchanged. It reaffirms the existing SSD controls: HMAC-keyed names, coordinator-authored cacheSalt, TTL, per-file AES-GCM authentication, and the epoch semantics. I saw no weakening of the T-041 mitigations. If the Nemotron Super owner ships with resident bank or SSD reuse, the T-041 sign-off scope (SEC-035) and the model-specific affected_files list may need updating. That is an unverified contract, not a finding.

build.md and test.md: they add 'Nemotron Super component qualification' sections for fixture harnesses (scripts/nemotron-qualification). They state that tiny-fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider. The sections add no new attack surface. They also reference a NEMOTRON_SUPER_REFERENCE_DIR env var, which is test-only. build.md (253-259) is placed before 'Related'; the placement is fine.

No threat-model invalidation found.
